This card is the whole of the task and it stands alone in front of a stranger. # Layer 3b: vec3, quat and transform as analyzer builtin types CONTEXT. moo (github.com/mas-bandwidth/moo, public, MIT) is Luau 0.741 made deterministic, with number = Q48.16 fixed point (the raw int64 of the C library fixed, vendored under extern/fixed at the fixed3d pin; never edit extern/). Read docs/DESIGN.md ("Layer 3 as built" and the section this card names) and docs/DETERMINISM.md before you start. The operators live in Common/include/moo_number.h, the parser in Common/include/moo_parse.h, the formatter in Common/include/moo_format.h, the C API boundary in VM/include/moo.h and VM/src/moo_api.cpp; moo's own tests are tests/Moo.test.cpp, tests/MooNumber.test.cpp and tests/Determinism.test.cpp (target Moo.Test) and tests/MooCompiler.test.cpp (in Luau.UnitTest); moo's expected-behaviour scripts are tests/conformance/moo/*.luau. WHERE YOUR TESTS AND NOTES GO. Card moo-l3-test-layout (landed before this one) makes Moo.Test build every tests/moo/*.test.cpp and tests/moo/*.c and run every tests/conformance/moo/l3/*.luau (each returns "OK"), with the moo_test helpers it documents in tests/MooHost.h. Put this card's new C++ cases in NEW tests/moo/moo-l3b-analyzer-types.test.cpp and its new scripts in NEW tests/conformance/moo/l3/moo-l3b-analyzer-types.luau (the l3 directory serves every layer), so no two cards edit one test registry. Do not edit docs/DESIGN.md or docs/DETERMINISM.md: write NEW docs/layer3b/moo-l3b-analyzer-types.md instead, holding the decision (if any) with its reason, what changed with file and function, and the exact sentences of DESIGN.md ("Layer 3 as built" and the section named) and DETERMINISM.md that must change; the layer's closing card (moo-l3b-conformance) folds every note into the two documents. Where this card's own text says to update DESIGN.md or DETERMINISM.md, that means this note. THE TASK. Declare the three types and their libraries in the embedded builtin definitions with the operator metatables (as vector's were: __add, __sub, __mul with the number overloads, __unm, __eq), and the library functions with their signatures exactly as the VM implements them (read moo_vec3lib.cpp, moo_quatlib.cpp, moo_transformlib.cpp). tests/conformance/types.luau then matches the VM's globals and the analyzer's definitions with no ignore. Tests: moo-analyze accepts a script using every function and operator, and reports a type error for vec3 + quat and for quat.slerp's absence if the VM refuses it.
